# PRB-002: Web ports do not answer on the raw IP behind a tunnel

- **Group:** Outside view
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

When a tunnel is the only intended ingress, the origin answering on 80 or 443 by IP lets anyone who finds that IP skip the tunnel and with it the WAF, access policies and rate limits (an origin bypass). stackward probe connects to 80 and 443 on every resolved address and sends GET / with the Host header set to the IP, without following redirects. For this raw IP check only, TLS certificate verification is skipped, because an IP has no certificate name to match; the report says so. This is the outside half of CF-005 and CF-003: if the host audit shows a tunnel and this check fails, the origin is bypassable. On a public web or panel profile answering is expected and reported as info; with the auto profile it is a warning, since only you know whether the host sits behind a tunnel.

## Verify by hand

```sh
curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --max-redirs 0 https://<origin-ip>/   # from another machine
```

## How to fix it

Publish the proxy on 127.0.0.1 only and let the tunnel connector reach it locally, then drop the public 80 and 443 rules in the provider firewall.

## What a fix can break

Anything reaching the proxy by IP stops working; check the tunnel serves every hostname first.

Run `stackward explain PRB-002` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
